about.title: Personal Injury Help in Riverbank, California
about.longDescription: Riverbank is a small city, but its roads carry real traffic — and real risk. In the most recent full year on record, Stanislaus County logged 103 injury collisions and 155 injured people connected to Riverbank-area crashes, with one traffic death. Corridors like Patterson Road, Oakdale Road, Claribel Road, and Rt 108 see the heaviest reported collision counts, and Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. tend to be when crash reports cluster. Those numbers are public record, not a judgment on any particular street — but they're a reminder that a routine drive can turn into a life-changing injury in seconds. If that's happened to you or someone you love, LawProactive can help you find direction. We're a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney — we are not a law firm, we don't decide your case, and we never charge you a fee. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover money. Filing deadlines in California are strict, so if you're considering next steps, it helps to act with reasonable speed rather than wait.

whyChoose.title: Why It Helps to Understand California Law

items.title: Two Years to Act
items.desc: California generally gives injured people two years from the date of the incident to file a personal injury claim. Claims against a government entity, like a city road agency, can require notice in as little as six months, so timing matters.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Erase Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the crash — your share of fault simply reduces the amount, it doesn't eliminate it.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages such as pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life, unlike some other states.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning their fee comes only from money they recover for you — if there's no recovery, you owe no attorney fee.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Riverbank?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit. If a government entity was involved, such as a road or public agency, the notice deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking your situation early.

items.question: Will I still be able to recover money if I was partly at fault?
items.answer: Likely yes. California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means your compensation is reduced by your percentage of fault rather than blocked entirely. An independent attorney can help evaluate how fault might be allocated in your case.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Riverbank?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher reported counts along Patterson Road, Oakdale Road, Claribel Road, and Rt 108, with Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. showing more reports than other times. These are neutral record counts, not a statement that any particular road or time is inherently unsafe.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: No. In ordinary California personal injury cases, there is no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. Compensation depends on the facts of your case, not a statutory ceiling.

items.question: What does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and we are not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in the network work on contingency, so they're only paid if you recover money.
